subject: Renewal proposal — doubling reserved pool to 32 GPUs with updated hourly rate
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@olivetech.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — capacity planning and options

Hi Jorge,

Thanks again for taking time earlier this week to review usage telemetry and the upcoming renewal. Based on OliveTech's production growth trends and the burst patterns you shared, we think a staged doubling of reserved capacity makes the most sense to keep 95th percentile tail latency under 250ms for your highest-priority workflows.

High-level options we can put on the table:
- Maintain current 16-GPU reserved pool and add burst on-demand capacity (no rate change).
- Double to a 32-GPU reserved pool with a revised per-hour reserved rate and a 30% discount for a 12‑month term.
- Step-up plan: start with 24 GPUs for 60 days, then commit to 32 GPUs if utilization stays above X%.

Can you confirm which approach you want us to formalize for procurement? If you prefer the 32-GPU commit we’ll send a detailed proposal with hourly economics and a throughput SLA.

Thanks,
Tessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Tessa Morgan | tessa.morgan@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192
Redwood Inference
From: Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@olivetech.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: OliveTech Procurement <purchasing@olivetech.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — capacity planning and options

Tessa,

Appreciate the options. We are leaning toward committing to 32 GPUs for the next year but need a clear per-hour reserved rate and a measurable throughput guarantee. A couple of constraints from my side:
- Procurement needs a flat per-hour line item (no complex blended hourly tiers).
- We need a throughput SLA that covers sustained sequence lengths up to 1024 tokens for our inference pipelines.
- Can you confirm any obligations around model quantization or cache invalidation windows that could affect latency?

If you can share a concrete proposal (PDF) with the hourly rate, monthly cap, and SLA language, I’ll fast-track with procurement.

— Jorge
Head of Engineering, OliveTech
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: OliveTech renewal — pricing and SLA asks (need numbers)

Team — forwarding Jorge's note. He wants: flat per-hour reserved rate for 32 GPUs, throughput SLA for seq<=1024, and confirmation on quantization/cache impacts. Draft quick answers below and tell me what to present: 

Rishi — for sustained seq<=1024, we can offer a SLO of 99.5% requests < 350ms P95 if they accept our KV-prefix caching and the suggested batching windows. Would you confirm that and whether we need an explicit carve-out for model warm-up bursts?

Monica — procurement will want the monthly cap and billing cadence. Can we propose a blended monthly cap that maps to the hourly rate but keeps billing simple for them?

Dev — any legal flags on offering explicit performance credits? We usually prefer service credits rather than hard SLAs for latencies.

Thanks,
Tessa
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2027 11:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: OliveTech renewal — pricing and SLA asks (need numbers)

On Thu, Sep 23, 2027 at 08:27, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Rishi — for sustained seq<=1024, we can offer a SLO of 99.5% requests < 350ms P95 if they accept our KV-prefix caching and the suggested batching windows. Would you confirm that and whether we need an explicit carve-out for model warm-up bursts?

Agree with the proposed SLO but recommend tightening wording: 99.5% of inference requests with sequence length <=1024 will have P95 latency under 350ms over a 30-day measurement window, provided default caching (prefix + KV) is enabled and request patterns don't exceed routable concurrency of the pool.

Warm-up carve-out: propose a 10-minute warm-up window per model version after cold-start, excluded from SLA measurements. For model quantization — we can support INT8/4-bit quantized instances. We'll call out that certain aggressive quant settings can increase latency variability by up to ~10% in microbenchmarks; include implementation guidance in the SLA appendix.

I'll attach a short technical appendix for the SLA and a recommended configuration for OliveTech's workloads.

-Rishi
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@olivetech.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: OliveTech — formal renewal proposal (32-GPU reserved pool)

Hi Jorge — attaching the formal proposal per your ask. Summary below and the attached PDF has line-item math plus the SLA appendix.

Summary proposal (clean line items for procurement):
- Commitment: 32 reserved GPUs (one-year term)
- Per-hour reserved rate: $11.50 / GPU-hour (flat line item; billed hourly, invoiced monthly)
- Monthly cap: 32 GPUs * 24 * 30 = 23,040 GPU-hours (invoiced at committed rate; overage at on-demand rate $18.75/GPU-hr)
- Throughput SLA: 99.5% of requests (seq <=1024) P95 < 350ms over a 30-day window (excludes 10-min model warm-ups and documented maintenance windows)
- Performance credits: Service credit up to 5% of monthly invoice for SLA breaches (capped and detailed in SLA appendix)
- On-boarding: Two-week migration assistance with priority scheduling.

Attachments: OliveTech_Renewal_Proposal_v2.pdf, Throughput_Guarantee_SLA.pdf

Next steps: If this looks acceptable, I can issue a DocuSign-ready order form (PDF) and we can route to procurement. Open to a 60-day step-up between 24→32 if you’d rather a phased approach — that would shift the monthly cap math but leave the per-hour committed rate as a target.

Best,
Tessa

Tessa Morgan | Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: OliveTech — formal renewal proposal (32-GPU reserved pool)

Tessa, Monica —

Thanks for the clear proposal. Procurement reviewed the line items and pricing; the flat per-hour rate is exactly what they needed for the PO. Legal wants the SLA appendix reviewed by our contracts team but nothing blocking. We do want to confirm one small change before signature: can you add a 90-day performance review checkpoint tied to utilization and the option to re-evaluate the monthly cap? This is just to make sure we can avoid a surprise overage at month-end as we migrate more production traffic.

If you can add that checkpoint to the order form (non-binding review), we’ll get the DocuSign executed this week.

-Jorge
Head of Engineering, OliveTech
